report.summary: During the 3‑hour investigation window, checkout‑service logged repeated Java OutOfMemoryError and GC overhead warnings while the resident memory metric remained steady per threshold‑validated data but raw query shows a 1× increase. The evidence points to heap exhaustion, likely caused by a memory leak or an insufficiently sized JVM heap.

likely_causes.title: Heap exhaustion due to a memory leak
likely_causes.rationale: The service logged four OutOfMemoryError events and sixteen GC overhead limit approaching warnings, indicating sustained high heap usage. The raw resident memory query shows a 1× increase, supporting the notion that the heap is growing beyond its capacity.

supporting_evidence.detail: ERROR checkout-service: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space (sample timestamps 2026-09-23T11:53:46+00:00 to 2026-09-23T12:14:46+00:00)
WARN checkout-service: GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92% (sample timestamps 2026-09-23T10:59:46+00:00 to 2026-09-23T12:14:46+00:00)
Raw resident memory rose 1.0x from 1337046606.80 to 1374168568.62 bytes

likely_causes.title: Insufficient JVM heap size configured
likely_causes.rationale: GC overhead limit approaching warnings are commonly triggered when the heap is too small for the workload. The absence of a sudden spike in the threshold‑validated metric suggests the heap may be consistently under‑provisioned rather than a transient leak.

next_steps: Collect and analyze heap dumps from checkout‑service during the incident window
Review recent code changes or deployments that could introduce memory leaks
Increase the JVM heap size and monitor for recurrence of OOM errors
Enable detailed GC logging to capture heap usage trends before and after the incident
